s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive respiratory distress with weight loss and systemic inflammation
salient_findings: Worsening dyspnea over 1 month
Unintentional 10-lb weight loss
Bilateral vesicular breathing with diffuse rhonchi on lung auscultation
Innumerable ill-defined nodular opacities within both lungs on CT Chest
Marked FDG-avid uptake at the lung lesion on PET scan
key_facts: Medical history of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
Bilateral vesicular breathing with diffuse rhonchi on lung auscultation
Respiratory viral panel, SARS-CoV-2 PCR, fungal pneumonia work-up were negative
QuantiFERON TB test, hepatitis panel, and HIV were nonreactive
CT Chest showed innumerable ill-defined nodular opacities within both lungs
PET scan showed marked FDG-avid uptake at the lung lesion, right neck lymph node, and left acetabular bone marrow
CT-guided lung biopsy revealed patchy areas of large atypical lymphoid cells with necrosis

shortlist.label: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Patchy areas of large atypical lymphoid cells with necrosis on CT-guided lung biopsy, consistent with lymphoma

shortlist.label: Lymphomatoid granulomatosis
shortlist.why_kept: Infiltration of lung parenchyma by malignant neoplasm with mixed inflammatory infiltrate and vascular involvement on VATS wedge resection

shortlist.label: Primary pulmonary lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Marked FDG-avid uptake at the lung lesion on PET scan, suggestive of malignant process

shortlist.label: Anaplastic large cell lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of large atypical lymphoid cells with necrosis on CT-guided lung biopsy, consistent with high-grade lymphoma

shortlist.label: Angioimmunoblastic T-cell lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Systemic inflammation and weight loss, with lymph node involvement on PET scan, raising suspicion for T-cell lymphoma

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with a large atypical lymphoid cell infiltration, marked nuclear pleomorphism, and atypical mitotic figures, along with the presence of a hilar mass and splenomegaly, is more consistent with a diagnosis of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma. The CT-guided lung biopsy and VATS wedge resection findings support this diagnosis.
raw.anchor_refutation: Lymphomatoid granulomatosis typically presents with a more gradual onset of symptoms, and the biopsy findings often show a more prominent granulomatous component, which is not seen in this case. The presence of large atypical lymphoid cells with necrosis and the lack of granulomatous features in the biopsy make lymphomatoid granulomatosis less likely.

rejected.label: Lymphomatoid granulomatosis
rejected.why: Lack of granulomatous features in biopsy and presence of large atypical lymphoid cells with necrosis

rejected.label: Primary pulmonary lymphoma
rejected.why: The presence of a hilar mass and splenomegaly, along with the PET scan findings, suggest a more systemic disease process, which is not typical of primary pulmonary lymphoma

rejected.label: Anaplastic large cell lymphoma
rejected.why: The biopsy findings do not show the characteristic CD30-positive cells or the presence of a t(2;5) translocation, which are often seen in anaplastic large cell lymphoma

rejected.label: Angioimmunoblastic T-cell lymphoma
rejected.why: The patient's presentation and biopsy findings do not show the characteristic features of angioimmunoblastic T-cell lymphoma, such as a polymorphous lymphoid infiltrate and the presence of arborizing vessels
